cards.text: Then a man is brought to Jesus, and friend, this man has a LOT going on. He's demon-possessed, he's blind AND he's mute.

cards.question: A demon-possessed man who can't see or speak is standing in front of Jesus. What happens?

answers.text: Jesus heals him so he can speak and see
Jesus sends him to the temple priests
Jesus tells him to come back tomorrow

cards.text: The crowds see the whole thing, and they are ASTOUNDED. People start asking a big question about who Jesus is.

cards.question: The crowds who saw Jesus heal the man are astounded. What do they start asking about Jesus?

answers.text: If He could be the Son of David
If He could be Elijah come back
If He could be John the Baptist

cards.text: But the Pharisees, a group of strict Jewish religious leaders, hear what the crowds are saying. And they've got a VERY different explanation.

cards.question: The Pharisees say Jesus drives out demons by the power of God.

cards.text: They say, “Only by Beelzebul, the prince of demons, does this man drive out demons.” A blind man sees. A mute man talks. And their takeaway is… demons.

cards.question: Jesus knows what the Pharisees are thinking. He answers with a picture of a kingdom divided against itself. What does He say happens to it?
Jesus says if Satan drives out Satan, he is divided against himself. What's the problem with that for Satan?

cards.text: Then Jesus flips it: if He drives out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do the Pharisees' own sons drive them out? Friend, that's the kind of question where everybody suddenly finds their shoes VERY interesting.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Pharisees that their own sons, who drive out demons too, will be their ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus gives the other option. What if He's driving out demons by the Spirit of God?

cards.question: Jesus says that if He drives out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon them.

cards.text: Then Jesus paints a picture: a strong man's house, and someone who wants to carry off everything inside. Friend, that strong man is NOT going to just hold the door open.

cards.question: In Jesus' picture, to plunder a strong man's house, you first have to ___ the strong man.

cards.text: Then Jesus makes it plain. There's no sitting on the fence with this one.

cards.question: Jesus says whoever is not with Him is ___ Him, and whoever does not gather with Him ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus gets serious. He says every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, except one.

cards.question: Jesus says every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, except one. Which blasphemy will not be forgiven?
The Son of Man is a name Jesus uses for Himself. Jesus says whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will not be forgiven.

cards.text: Jesus says, “Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the one to come.”
Then Jesus switches to trees. Make a tree good and its fruit will be good, make it bad and its fruit will be bad.

cards.question: In Jesus' picture of the good tree and the bad tree, how is a tree known?

answers.text: By the roots it puts down

cards.text: Then Jesus says to the Pharisees, “You brood of vipers, how can you who are evil say anything good?” Friend, that is NOT a pep talk.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Pharisees the words a mouth speaks come out of the overflow of something. What is it?

cards.text: Then Jesus says the good man brings good things out of his good store of treasure. Same as my cookie boxes, friend: you only get out what got packed in.

cards.question: In Jesus' picture, the evil man brings good things out of his evil store of treasure.

cards.text: Then Jesus talks about the words people speak and the day of judgment. Friend, I talk a LOT, so I am leaning ALL the way in on this one.

cards.question: Jesus says men will give an account on the day of judgment for every ___ word they have spoken.
Jesus finishes: by your words you will be ___, and by your words you will be ___.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Jesus tells him to come back tomorrow" isn't believable for this moment. It reads as silly next to the other two answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The punchline "And their takeaway is… demons" laughs at the Pharisees' reasoning instead of looking at their human situation with respect.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: The card retells the healing ("A blind man sees. A mute man talks.") from Matthew 12:22 but cites only Matthew 12:24. It should cite Matthew 12:22-24.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: No story card sets up Jesus' reply. Jesus knowing their thoughts and the divided-kingdom picture are told for the first time inside the question. The city and household half of Matthew 12:25 is never told at all.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is on a story card.

findings.problem: No story card tells the Satan-driving-out-Satan line before this card. The question is the first place the baker meets it.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is on a story card. Not every choice card needs its own story card right before it: a choice card can follow another choice card when the setup is already told.

findings.problem: The question spends words explaining what "Son of Man" means. That belongs in a dictionary pop-up.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: Most of this card restates what cards 1 through 3 already told and asked (Son of Man forgiven, Holy Spirit not forgiven). Only "either in this age or in the one to come" is new.
The blank asks the baker to guess the exact word "careless." Card 11 gives nothing to reason from, and "angry" fits the question just as well.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Nothing in the question tells the baker which blank gets "acquitted" and which gets "condemned." Swapping them is just as reasonable, so the order is pure wording recall.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Several story cards are flat narration with no Papa Dorin reaction or laugh: stop 1 cards 12 and 16, and stop 2 cards 1, 4 and 5. Across the walkthrough, the funny moments are thin.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
